purpose: Fresh, broad sustainability audit of representative public visitor tasks using current live evidence and explicitly selected owner-supplied source

protocol.states: Initial desktop, then same document resized to 360 CSS px, live reduced-motion and dark changes, print emulation, twelve Tab presses; separate fresh no-JavaScript and dark contexts. Resized and emulated states are not independent cold loads or real-device tests.
protocol.measurementPurpose: Qualitative review and bounded interaction evidence, not headline bytes or energy
limitations: Main document observations; embedded frames are not traversed
Page probes include bounded Tab traversal after other states; no control activation. Journey actions must be explicit
Selected CDP response headers omit cookies and authorization; no header alone proves cache reuse
Keyboard trace is twelve Tab presses, not complete keyboard or accessibility conformance
Resource Timing zeros may reflect timing restrictions or cache, not zero traffic
Notification requestPermission calls counted with a delegating wrapper
Print emulation is not PDF pagination or document accessibility testing

checkDefinitions.expectation: Assess visible distractions against the declared visitor task; distinguish useful prompts from interruptions.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Inspect choice wording, defaults, prominence and the observed accept/reject paths for undue steering. DOM text alone does not establish visual parity.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Assess the sampled task's wording, headings and terminology for its stated audience; retain uncertainty about unrepresented users.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Compare repeated navigation and control names across sampled pages; consistent samples do not prove a documented design system.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Assess observed animation purpose, playback controls and reduced-motion behavior. A quiet snapshot does not prove no motion occurs elsewhere.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Assess observed alerts and notification permission requests for user value and choice; absence is limited to observed states.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Review print layout visibility and download labels for the declared task. Fetch and inspect document content before asserting optimization or equivalence.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Use initial JS/CSS execution observations to nominate investigation targets; require representative journeys or source corroboration before recommending removal.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Relate initial script resources to visible components and later task needs; recommend splitting only when a component's deferred use and usable activation are corroborated.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Compare narrow and desktop task content and overflow, then exercise affected controls; width emulation alone is not real-device compatibility.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Identify consequential user choices in the sample and assess whether contextual impact information is useful and supported. Do not prescribe carbon labels on every control.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Execute declared task actions and inspect completion evidence; an expected selector is one observable, not proof of user success or optimal journey length.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled task images preserve useful content and provide proportionate intrinsic dimensions and delivery choices for their rendered size and pixel density. A large image is an investigation candidate until legibility and task value are checked; absent srcset alone is not a failure.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Compare desktop/narrow image dimensions, srcset/sizes, delivered MIME types, loading state, and task content. Confirm any proposed rendition at intended pixel densities before asserting savings.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Observed web fonts and variants serve the sampled content, with a declared fallback/loading strategy where needed. Do not fail a site merely for using a web font; recommend removal or subsetting only after language and readability requirements are established.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Inspect document.fonts family/weight/style/display/status, font responses and visible body text. Missing font-blocking/constrained-loading or language evidence can leave the scoped judgment unresolved.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled document has a meaningful language, primary heading and main region, and task controls have visible labels or an explicit naming relationship. Count/attribute presence alone does not establish semantic correctness or WCAG compliance.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Read title/lang/headings/mainCount, form control labels and task content. aria-labelledby references need resolution before claiming a missing accessible name.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled content has a descriptive title and usable canonical metadata when applicable; declared structured-data blocks parse as JSON. Judge description and other optional metadata according to page purpose, not a mandatory-field checklist.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Inspect metadata and document title, resolving canonical URLs and applicability. JSON parsing does not establish schema validity or search-engine eligibility.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled page respects applicable dark/reduced-motion preferences both before navigation and when they change in-page, without losing task content. Distinguish intentional design choices and absence of applicable motion from unsupported behavior.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled core reading content and navigation remain available without JavaScript, or an explicit alternative supports the task. This bounded check does not establish no-JavaScript search, every interaction, or all browser compatibility.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Compare desktop and fresh no_javascript text/headings/navigation. Explain task-critical missing content and legitimate progressive enhancements rather than demanding every feature without scripts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Repeated observed API requests are justified by the sampled task and its update needs. Identify redundant-looking requests for investigation without inferring backend cost or safe removal from URL repetition alone.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Inspect bounded network.requests methods/types/timestamps and explicit journey resource entries. Establish polling purpose, cache behavior and task freshness needs; initial-only windows may remain cantTell.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Reusable public scripts/styles/media expose an appropriate caching or validation policy in the sample. Distinguish dynamic/private responses and note that headers alone do not prove cache reuse or offline support.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Review allowlisted response cache-control/etag/last-modified/age/vary headers and public resource purpose. Require a warm-load test before claiming measured reuse; private no-store is a legitimate exception.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Material sampled text assets are delivered with compression where beneficial. Do not demand compression for already-compressed images, tiny bodies or error responses without context.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Review text/script/style response MIME types, status and content-encoding, alongside transfer magnitude when available. Header absence for a material text response supports investigation; missing response evidence stays unknown.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled initial keyboard path reaches visible task navigation/controls in a meaningful order with a discernible focus indicator. A bounded Tab trace cannot establish complete keyboard support, reverse navigation, traps or screen-reader accessibility.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Inspect keyboardFocus steps, names/label relationships, element geometry, focus-visible and outline clues. A zero outline is not proof of invisible focus because borders or shadows may supply it; verify the actual indicator before a failure.

Add, edit, and remove images

If you want to edit, add, or remove images from the Admin interface outside of the individual pages, you can do so from the Images interface. To access the Images interface, click Images in the Sidebar.

Wagtail allows you to select multiple images from the Images interface at once. To do this, select the checkbox on the top left of each image block, then use the bulk actions bar at the bottom to perform an action on all selected images.

Also, Wagtail allows you to edit the data associated with an image by clicking on the image to access its edit screen. Image data includes the title, the file, the collection associated with it, the associated tags, and the focal area.

List layout

In addition to the default “grid” layout, this interface also supports viewing images in a list, like other listings. This can be useful when working with larger numbers of images.

Image alt text

By default, Wagtail uses the image’s description field as alt text. Alt text is important for screen reader users accessing the site but also the CMS, to get a text description of the image contents.

It is also common for site implementers to customize this, either by adding a separate alt text field for all images, or where images are used.

So, to help screen reader users better understand your images, ensure you provide image descriptions or explicitly mark images that are purely decorative.

Warning

Changing the file will change it on all pages that use the image.

Set the focal area of an image

The Images interface allows you to set a focal area, which can affect how your image displays to visitors on the front end. If you crop your images in some way to make them fit into a specific shape, then the focal area defines the centre point from which you crop the images.

You can set the focal area of an image by clicking the image to access its edit screen. Then drag a marquee around the most significant element of the image, and then click Save to save it. Once you set the focal area of an image and save it, you can see the most significant element of the image on the front end.

To remove the focal area, click Remove focal area in the edit screen.

Image format requirements

By default, Wagtail supports image uploads in the following file formats: AVIF, GIF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP. Site implementers can also allow fewer formats, or add support for HEIC / HEIF. Wagtail will then convert images to the appropriate format for site users based on configuration by developers.

Wagtail also optimizes image quality based on the needs of site users, per the configuration done by developers. By default, images use a "safe for web" quality setting to apply compression suitable for most use cases from thumbnails to photography. Developers can override this default configuration wherever images are in use, or even display images with "lossless" quality.

File size requirements

By default, Wagtail limits image uploads to a maximum of 10MB. It also restricts uploading of images larger than 128 megapixels (close to 16K resolution).

Here are highlights from Wagtail 8.1. For full technical details, view the complete v8.1 release notes.

Wagtail Space 2026

Our flagship Wagtail Space conference returns! Coming up 18-20 November, a free virtual event for people who are improving the world through code and content. 22 presentations over two days of talks and one day of community events. Register to join us 🚀

SEO power tools: page metadata

The Checks panel and the userbar's Checks dialog now show each page's meta title and meta description, with their length measured against how search engines typically display them. You can also expand View more meta tags to inspect every tag that search engines and social media link previews will see.

This makes it much easier to spot titles and descriptions that search engines will truncate, providing feedback on drafts without a need for separate tools that only work on published pages.

Thank you to Freedom of the Press Foundation for their sponsorship of this feature!

Varying page responses

When configured by a developer, Wagtail can now serve more than one version of the content of a page at the same URL. This general-purpose capability can be used for content negotiation: for example to serve structured data with APIs, or Markdown for AI agents as a form of agent readiness. Here is an example rendering a page as Markdown:

API v3 for structured content

The v3 API preview gained a large batch of improvements since Wagtail 8.0, most notably:

Table blocks and nested inline relations can now be created and updated through the API, rather than needing to be edited in the Admin interface.
More complete schemas: the API now self-documents more of your content model.
More reliable Markdown: rich text is converted to Markdown more consistently, particularly styled text inside links, line breaks, multi-paragraph quotes, and nested lists. This makes the Markdown output of pages far closer to what you see on the site.

Here is an example of the structured schema, with the fields of a specific body block clearly visible:

As in Wagtail 8.0, all of this needs a developer to enable the API. For developer documentation, see the v3 API guide.

API v3 workflow operations

The API now supports workflow operations on pages and and compatible snippets, so integrations can submit content to a workflow without visiting the Admin interface.

Faster, better sitemaps for multilingual sites

Sitemaps now include alternate links for translated pages, and list every locale of the site rather than only the default one. If you run a multilingual site, more of your translated content can be discovered by search engines.

Prototype command line interface (CLI)

As part of the new v3 API preview, we are introducing a prototype Wagtail CLI to speed up and automate common operations on Wagtail projects. When the API is set up by a developer, CMS users can then use the command line interface to make content changes.

Official agent skills

We now provide official agent skills for developers, that work together with the CLI and the API. They are primarily intended for developers but also make AI agents work more effectively on all Wagtail-related tasks.

Here is an example that combines the CLI, the skills, and the API to make content changes with DeepSeek Harness and Mistral Large 4.

Other UI improvements

This release also includes a range of smaller enhancements that improve day-to-day editing:

When you move or rename a page, Wagtail no longer creates a redirect if the page isn't live, and no longer creates one if its URL doesn't actually change.
The document upload form now lists the file types it accepts, so you know what's supported before choosing a file.
Moving or renaming a page now clears the relevant pages from your site's front-end cache, so visitors see the updated address sooner.
Uploaded avatars respect the orientation stored in the photo, so portrait photos no longer appear sideways in the Admin interface.
Workflow action buttons are protected against double clicks, which could previously cause an error or overwrite another person's decision.
Workflow actions are rejected if the task was updated by someone else while you were filling it in, rather than overwriting their change.
In the slim Sidebar, nested submenu labels no longer become invisible.
Copying a page with a long revision history no longer uses excessive memory.
Audit log entries for copying pages, copying for translation, and creating aliases now reference the page you copied rather than its parent page.
Rich text content is more reliable in the v3 API's Markdown output, particularly around links, line breaks, quotes, and nested lists.

Many behind-the-scenes fixes and performance improvements are also included.

Let us know what you think

We thrive with feedback from our community. Make sure to register for Wagtail Space 2026, and tell us how you find the new release!

The User Guide is a website to help content editors, moderators, administrators, and other users learn how to use Wagtail, the leading open source Python content management system (CMS). It’s comprehensive documentation for CMS users, including reference information on the admin features, how-tos, and more.

AI-friendly documentation

For users of Large Language Models (LLMs) and agents, the user guide contents are available in machine-friendly formats:

Markdown content negotiation for all pages.
llms.txt, an LLM-focused index of all site contents.
llms-full.txt, a full copy of the documentation
Wagtail guide support skill, an opinionated agent skill you can copy-paste into your preferred AI tool so it answers questions based on the site’s contents.
WebMCP, so you can navigate the docs with your agent.
OpenAPI API, to retrieve the website’s contents programmatically.

The site follows the Agentic Resource Discovery specification to make this information available.

Historical copies

Historical copies of the site contents are available in our Git repository, so you can browse or compare how the documentation has changed over time. See the content directory in the wagtail/guide repository, with the historical source of every page.

Add, edit, and remove images

If you want to edit, add, or remove images from the Admin interface outside of the individual pages, you can do so from the Images interface. To access the Images interface, click Images in the Sidebar.

Wagtail allows you to select multiple images from the Images interface at once. To do this, select the checkbox on the top left of each image block, then use the bulk actions bar at the bottom to perform an action on all selected images.

Also, Wagtail allows you to edit the data associated with an image by clicking on the image to access its edit screen. Image data includes the title, the file, the collection associated with it, the associated tags, and the focal area.

List layout

In addition to the default “grid” layout, this interface also supports viewing images in a list, like other listings. This can be useful when working with larger numbers of images.

Image alt text

By default, Wagtail uses the image’s description field as alt text. Alt text is important for screen reader users accessing the site but also the CMS, to get a text description of the image contents.

It is also common for site implementers to customize this, either by adding a separate alt text field for all images, or where images are used.

So, to help screen reader users better understand your images, ensure you provide image descriptions or explicitly mark images that are purely decorative.

Warning

Changing the file will change it on all pages that use the image.

Set the focal area of an image

The Images interface allows you to set a focal area, which can affect how your image displays to visitors on the front end. If you crop your images in some way to make them fit into a specific shape, then the focal area defines the centre point from which you crop the images.

You can set the focal area of an image by clicking the image to access its edit screen. Then drag a marquee around the most significant element of the image, and then click Save to save it. Once you set the focal area of an image and save it, you can see the most significant element of the image on the front end.

To remove the focal area, click Remove focal area in the edit screen.

Image format requirements

By default, Wagtail supports image uploads in the following file formats: AVIF, GIF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP. Site implementers can also allow fewer formats, or add support for HEIC / HEIF. Wagtail will then convert images to the appropriate format for site users based on configuration by developers.

Wagtail also optimizes image quality based on the needs of site users, per the configuration done by developers. By default, images use a "safe for web" quality setting to apply compression suitable for most use cases from thumbnails to photography. Developers can override this default configuration wherever images are in use, or even display images with "lossless" quality.

File size requirements

By default, Wagtail limits image uploads to a maximum of 10MB. It also restricts uploading of images larger than 128 megapixels (close to 16K resolution).
